mechanism_narrative: Because WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain deeply below baseline while RETAIL_REC is only slightly less negative than four weeks ago, continued return-to-work commuting should still raise retail visits over the next month. If workplace attendance and transit use stop recovering, the retail gain will not materialize.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the last 4 weeks even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve for at least two consecutive weekly observations.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week jump in PARKS mobility of at least 5 points shifts discretionary outings toward outdoor leisure and away from shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks. If the park surge is only temporary or not accompanied by substitution away from indoor venues, retail will not weaken.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 14 days after a PARKS week-on-week increase of 5 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL holds above baseline while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay suppressed, mobility substitution toward home-based activity persists and retail traffic remains weak over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails when outside-the-home activity broadens beyond commuting restrictions.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above baseline and both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run improvement in GROCERY_PHARM often precedes broader errand chaining: when shopping trips are already returning, nearby retail and recreation activity follows within one week. If grocery mobility stalls or reverses, the retail spillover disappears.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0% and stays positive for two weekly readings
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve in the next 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM remains above baseline for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS falls while TRANSIT stays weak, discretionary travel is not expanding; this combination signals lingering caution and should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent 4-week mean over the next month. The claim fails if retail strengthens without a simultaneous transit rebound.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days even though PARKS remains weak and TRANSIT does not recover.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL time after staying elevated indicates people are leaving home more often, which should lift retail visits over the next two weeks. If home-stay behavior does not fall, retail will not gain from this seasonal mobility release.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls at least 0.5 points week-on-week from an above-baseline level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL falls from an elevated level.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays below baseline but TRANSIT begins rising, commuting is resuming faster than office attendance, and retail spending should improve with a one-to-two week lag as travel corridors reactivate. The effect fails when transit remains flat or workplaces do not follow.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises while WORKPLACES remains below -10%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 14 days after TRANSIT rises while WORKPLACES stays below -10%.

mechanism_narrative: A stronger PARKS rebound combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM indicates a shift into weather-driven leisure rather than necessity trips, which should reduce retail-and-recreation shopping traffic over the next four weeks. If grocery activity also weakens, the leisure substitution signal is not strong enough to depress retail.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -20% while GROCERY_PHARM stays between -5% and +5%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite PARKS improving above -20% and GROCERY_PHARM remaining near baseline.
